best_known_lineage.reason: Best available measured policy: 197/200 = 98.5% on the protected task-reference panel, the first campaign measurement at or above the 98% objective on that independent human-owned panel, and 194/200 = 97.0% on the researcher 200-episode panel, tied with working on the researcher panel and above it on task-reference. The margin is a single episode and the researcher-panel estimate remains below threshold with a systematic rear wedge that includes trained-radius failures, so terminal assessment is not requested; the designation records the strongest measured policy while development continues.

code.reason: The joint-limit proximity penalty changed no measured outcome on either development panel while slightly perturbing trajectories, so it adds nothing to the working science; the experiment-8 recipe (full official 6-20 cm radius training) is restored as the complete working recipe.

last_lineage_decision.reason: Experiment 9's joint-limit proximity penalty produced no measurable task change and is not a better continuation base than the parent. All three measured checkpoints (20,480, 100,352, 120,832 steps) reproduce the parent's exact researcher-panel failure set {7, 56, 64, 75, 107, 145} at 194/200 = 97.0%, and the endpoint ties the experiment-8 endpoint on the protected task-reference panel at 197/200 = 98.5% with the same failures {84, 102, 175}. The new joint-margin diagnostics show the penalized state is genuinely reached and fully active (every wedge failure pushes the closest joint 3.3-4.1 degrees past the +/-170 degree limit and incurs the maximum 0.05 per-step penalty, while only 9-10 of 194 successes do), so the inert outcome favors an optimization/credit-assignment limit at the shoulder boundary over the absence of a joint-limit signal, and it scopes the tested penalty magnitude and shape as insufficient. The campaign therefore continues from the stronger experiment-8 policy (working/best_known checkpoint-120832) rather than from any experiment-9 artifact.
